title: Synthesis of Infectious Bacteriophages in an E. coli-based Cell-free Expression System
protocol: Inoculate 10 mL Luria-Bertani (LB) media in a 15 mL culture tube with E. coli host cells, e.g., B or K12.
Incubate the inoculated culture at 37 °C on a shaker set to 250 rpm overnight to grow to saturation.
Warm several LB-agar plates at 37°C for 1 hour.
Prepare dilutions of phage stock in LB media, aiming for ~102-103 phage/mL.
Add 100 μL of overnight growth of concentrated host cells to each plate.
Choose volumes of the prepared phage dilutions corresponding to a range from 10-100 phage/plate.
Add required volume of phage dilutions to each plate (e.g., 100 µL of 103 phage/mL).
Incubate plates at 37°C and begin a count-up timer (+0 h).
Incubate for 4-5 hours.
Prepare 49 mL LB media in a 250 mL flask.
Place the flask on a rotary shaker set to 250 rpm and 37°C.
At +2.5 hours, dilute cells 50x by adding 1 mL of saturated cell culture into pre-warmed flask containing 49 mL LB medium.
Once cells reach log growth (+4-5 h), measure absorbance at 600 nm (OD600).
Determine the concentration of cells using conversion OD600 of 1.0 = 8 x 10^8 cell/mL.
Dilute to 2 x 10^7 cell/mL using additional LB growth media.
Remove agar plate containing phage plaques from incubator.
Use sterile Pasteur pipette to core and remove a single plaque.
Blow the plaque into diluted cells.
Incubate at 37°C for an additional 2 hours (+6-7 h).
Take a 500 µL sample into a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 10 µL chloroform to the sample.
Vortex at high speed immediately after adding chloroform.
Observe if the solution has clarified.
Incubate cells for another 2 h (+8-9 h) once fully infected.
If cells lyse, add DNase to a concentration of 5 µg/mL.
Centrifuge cells at 8,000 x g at 4 °C to pellet them.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of 1x TRIS magnesium chloride (TM) buffer with 5 µg/mL DNase.
Add 500 µL of chloroform to the resuspended sample.
Vortex at high speed immediately after adding chloroform.
Clarify by centrifugation at 12,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Decant the supernatant into a 15 mL conical tube and store at 4 °C.
Prepare 4x 5-45% sucrose gradients by pipetting 2.5 mL of 45% sucrose into 4 ultracentrifuge tubes.
Top each tube with ~2.6 mL of 5% sucrose, stopping when liquid reaches 2 mm from the rim of the tube.
Mix the gradients by tilt-tube rotation using a gradient forming instrument for 43 s at 86° at 23 rpm.
Remove 500 μL from the top of each prepared sucrose gradient with a 1 mL pipettor and balance to within ± 0.002 g.
Pool phage suspensions from all tubes.

Add 500 μL of the suspension by bringing the tip into contact with liquid surface and very slowly dispensing the volume onto the top of the sucrose gradient, being careful to not mix through rapid pipetting.
Centrifuge at 70,000 x g for 20 min at 4 °C.
Remove the phage bands using a sterile syringe and blunt cannula.
Submerge a blunt cannula into the solution until the tip is centered on the very upper edge of the phage band.
Remove the majority of the phage band by drawing on the syringe plunger.
Add the sucrose volume with the suspended phage to 3-4 ultracentrifuge tubes, adding no more than 1.5 mL per tube.
Fill each tube to approximately 3-4 mm from the top with cold 1x TM.
Cover each tube with paraffin film and invert to mix thoroughly.
Place the tubes in an ultracentrifuge and spin at 145,000 x g for 1 hour at 4 °C.
Quickly pour off the supernatant and drain upside down on disposable wipes.
Wipe the inside of each tube with a sterile cotton swab to remove excess supernatant.
Divide 200-400 µL cold 1x TM across all pellets and resuspend overnight at 4 °C without shaking.
If the pellet is not clean, pool and perform additional centrifugation in a microcentrifuge at 17,000 x g.
Prepare a culture of E. coli host cells in 10 mL LB growth media and leave it in a shaking incubator set to 250 rpm and 37 °C overnight.
Incubate the appropriate amount of culture plates at 37 °C for at least 1 hour before making titers of the phage stock.
Prepare 100 mL of top agar by adding 2.5 g LB and 0.6 g bacto-agar to a 100 mL bottle.
Autoclave the mixture after dissolving the solids in deionized water.
Invert the bottle 6-8 times to homogenize the agar solution.
Place the bottle in a 45 °C water bath for 15-20 min to equilibrate temperature.
Dilute phage stocks with LB solution by adding 990 μL LB to 10 μL phage stock for a 100-fold dilution, vortexing thoroughly.
For a 10-fold dilution, add 100 μL of phage stock to 900 μL LB and vortex thoroughly.
Repeat the dilution series as needed to obtain countable plaques (10-100 plaques).
Prepare an area for phage titers by assembling culture tubes equal in number to the phage stock dilutions.
Place diluted phage samples and host bacterial cells on ice.
Pipette 5.25 mL top agar, 220 μL diluted phage samples, and 50 μL host bacterial cells into a culture tube.
Cap the culture tube and vortex at high speed.
Store remaining phage solution at 4 °C.
Retrieve two culture plates from the 37 °C incubator.
Add 2.5 mL of master mix slowly to the center of the first plate without introducing bubbles.
Gently rotate the first plate by hand to distribute the master mix evenly across the entire surface.
Repeat with the second plate, adding 2.5 mL of master mix and rotating it evenly.
Wait 20 min for the top agar to solidify in both plates.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C for 4-7 hours.
Count the plaques appearing as 1-2 mm clear circles on the opaque background of host cells.
Dilute a portion of phage stock from step 2.9 to 400 µL with 1x TM buffer in a fresh 1.5 mL tube.
Add an equal volume of Tris:Phenol:Chloroform to the dilution.
Shake the mixture gently on a laboratory rocker, or by hand, for 5 min.
Centrifuge the resultant emulsion at 17,000 x g in a benchtop centrifuge for 5-10 min.
Remove the upper aqueous phase to a new tube, taking care not to disturb the interphase boundary.
Repeat steps for an additional 2 times for a total of 3 phenol extractions.
Transfer the aqueous phase to a fresh tube and add an equal volume of CHCl3.
Shake and centrifuge.
Transfer the aqueous DNA sample to a clean tube.
Estimate the volume of purified DNA.
Add 0.4 volumes of 3 M sodium acetate (CH3COONa) and 3 volumes of 95% ethanol (EtOH).
Place in -20 °C freezer for overnight precipitation.
Centrifuge at 17,000 x g for 10-15 min.
Remove and discard the supernatant either by decanting or pipetting.
Add 500 µL 70% EtOH and gently shake the tube until the pellet floats free from the bottom of the tube.
Centrifuge at 17,000 x g for 5 min.
Remove and discard EtOH, taking care to not disturb the pellet.
Repeat step of adding 70% EtOH and centrifuging.
Air dry the pellet on benchtop for 30-60 min.
Add 50 µL ddH2O to the pellet and incubate for 1 h at RT or overnight at 4 °C to resuspend.
Prepare 25 g LB medium and 15 g bacto-agar solid, pour into a 1 L bottle.
Add deionized water to the 1 L mark in the bottle.
Autoclave the contents of the bottle.
Invert the bottle slowly 6-8 times after sterilization to homogenize the agar solid throughout the solution.
Place the bottle in a 58 °C water bath for 20 min before dispensing onto culture plates.
Add 25 mL from the bottle into a 100 mm x 15 mm culture plate.
Set one culture plate aside and let it solidify for at least 1 h at room temperature.
Let the other 39 culture plates solidify for 2 days at room temperature.
Store the culture plates at 4 °C or use them immediately to make titers.
Plate the host cells by streaking an appropriate bacterial strain stored at -80 °C onto a LB-agar culture plate next to an open flame.
Incubate the plated cells overnight at 37 °C.
Prepare crude E. coli extract as previously described.
Mix crude E. coli extract, reaction buffer, and phage genome to achieve final concentrations of 8.9-9.9 mg/mL protein, 3-6 mM Mg-glutamate, 40-100 mM K-glutamate, and 2-4% PEG 8000.
Add 3-4 mM of each amino acid to the reaction mixture as previously described.
Mix in energy mix solution composed of DTT, HEPES, ATP, GTP, CTP, UTP, tRNA, CoA, NAD, cAMP, folinic acid, spermidine, and 3-PGA as per previous protocols.
Adjust final reaction volume to between 10-20 μL for optimal oxygenation.
Add additional component to inhibit recBCD enzyme digestion of linear DNA pieces if using linear genome molecules.
Complete the "reaction details" section in Table 1 by entering the total number of reactions and final volume of reaction.
Determine the constant and variable components of the reaction for experimental design.
Enter the fractional volume percentage of the master mix, which is the ratio of the total volume of the constant reaction components to the product of the final reaction volume and number of samples.
Enter the stock and final concentrations of the reaction reagents in the "Master Mix Reaction Recipe" section.
Enter the stock and final concentrations of the variable reagent(s) to be tested.
Remove the necessary amount of tubes (indicated in the "Tubes to thaw" section) of crude cell extract, energy buffer mix, and amino acid mix from -20 °C or -80 °C and thaw on ice.
Once thawed, combine multiple aliquots of like components if necessary.
Aliquot 33% of the final reaction volume of crude extract into a microcentrifuge tube.
Prepare the master mix as per Table 1.
Homogenize all components under "Master Mix Reaction Recipe" by vortexing.
Add the appropriate volume of each component to the crude extract.
Add 1 µM of the gam protein of bacteriophage lambda to the reaction.
Vortex to homogenize the solution, and place the reaction on ice for 5 min.
Split the master mix into n microcentrifuge tubes.
Incubate the microcentrifuge tubes at 29 °C for at least 8 h or overnight.
Inoculate a culture tube of 5 mL LB with 3-5 healthy host cell colonies using a sterile pipette tip.
Incubate the culture tube in a shaking incubator at 37 °C and 250 rpm for 16 h or overnight.
Dispense 50 mL LB into a 500 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Cover the flask with aluminum foil.
Warm the flask at 37 °C for 20 min.
Aliquot 1 mL of the host cell overnight pre-culture into the pre-warmed LB.
Incubate for 3-4 h at 37 °C and shaking at 250 rpm.
Centrifuge the 50 mL host cell culture for 10 min at 5,000 x g.
Discard the LB.
Resuspend the pellet with cold (4 °C) 5 mL LB.
Keep the resuspended cells on ice.
Incubate the culture plates at 37 °C one hour before starting the titer experiment.
Prepare a serial dilution of the cell-free reaction with LB solution as described in section 2.12.
Titer the final cell-free reaction-LB solution as described in section 2, steps 2.14-2.16.
